Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the chase! The players are already out in the middle now. Phil Salt and Jos Buttler are the explosive opening pair for England. West Indies going with spin, as Akeal Hosein will start proceedings with the ball. Here we go...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Rashid shines as England leak runs late - England started well with the ball, with Curran and Holder striking early, while Overton also picked up a wicket in his first over. But they could not contain the Windies onslaught through the middle overs, except for Adil Rashid, who was brilliant with figures of 4-0-16-2. However, Rashid's drop of Rutherford may have cost them a few more towards the end. Overton did add another to his tally, but the pacers were taken apart at the death, making the job for the batters a tough one now. However, England still have enough firepower and quality, and we are in for an exciting chase. Join us in a bit for the second essay.

Windies rebuild and explode - Despite a couple of early setbacks, Rutherford continued his good form with a brisk cameo as the Windies reached 55 for 3 at the end of the Powerplay. However, Sherfane Rutherford was at the heart of the effort, smashing it all around the park to finish unbeaten on 76 off 42, his highest T20I score. Rutherford put on a couple of fifty-plus partnerships, first with Powell and then with Holder, whose quickfire 33 off 17 played a key role, while Chase also showed his value with the bat by steadying things after the early loss of wickets.

West Indies finish with a flourish - A power-packed batting display from West Indies, exactly what they are known for in this format. There were a few tricky phases, but they muscled their way through them and finished strongly, smashing 29 runs off the last two overs. England's death bowling has come back to haunt them again, and it will be a stiff target to chase with no signs of dew as yet.

SIX! Rutherford finishes in style! Full and outside off, Sherfane Rutherford finds the ball in his wheelhouse and bulldozes it over long off for a cracking six. 14 runs from the final over. WEST INDIES FINISH ON 196/6.

Commentary.Commentary: Adil Rashid comes into the attack right after the end of the Powerplay. He was taken to the cleaners by Nepal in the last game, 3-0-42-0, and would be looking to redeem himself.
Spears one at off, on a fullish length, Sherfane Rutherford commits on the back foot and dabs it to short third and it is fielded well there. West Indies are 55/3 at the end of the Powerplay.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.6: Jamie Overton to Sherfane Rutherford, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: DRINKS! West Indies have scored at a brisk rate till now, but the problem for them is that they have lost three key batters as well. Hetmyer was looking good, but could not convert his start, and now the pressure will be on the Windies' middle order to deliver against a strong opposition. England will be happy with how things are going, but know that they cannot take it lightly, as the Men in Maroon do bat deep, and most of them can take the game away with their power-hitting. Also, Sherfane Rutherford is the next man in.

OUT! TAKEN! England have Hetmyer's wicket. This is a well-directed short ball, dug into the pitch with pace taken off slightly, on top of the stumps. It lands and kicks up further. Shimron Hetmyer goes for the pull shot, but the ball gets big on him and it is sliced off the top edge. The ball goes to the moon and sails towards short fine leg. Sam Curran lurks under it and takes a straightforward catch. The 47-run partnership is broken.
Commentary.Howout: c Sam Curran b Jamie Overton
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.5: Jamie Overton to Shimron Hetmyer, OUT! c Sam Curran b Jamie Overton.

Commentary.Commentary: Cannoned in and around the pads, on a fuller length. Shimron Hetmyer looks to whip that across, but misses and the ball deflects off the pads, rolls past the stumps toward the right of short fine and they hurry back and get two leg byes.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.4: Jamie Overton to Shimron Hetmyer, 2 Leg byes.

Commentary.Commentary: Hard length ball on the off pole, it hits the bat hard and Hetmyer ends up chopping it towards short third. Denies the single and sends Chase back.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.3: Jamie Overton to Shimron Hetmyer, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Length ball, on the leg stump, clipped away to the leg side for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.2: Jamie Overton to Roston Chase, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Change of gloves for Shimron Hetmyer, after putting in that dive.

Chance of a run out, missed! Pitched up, full and on leg, Roston Chase chips it on the bounce to mid on. Hetmyer wants a single, but Chase sends him as Archer is quick to get rid of the ball, but misses his shy at the bowling end. Shimron puts a dive in and gets home. But a direct hit would have had Hettie rushing back to the dugout.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.1: Jamie Overton to Roston Chase, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: A 14-run over is followed by an over going for 19 runs. West Indies have struck back strongly after losing both their openers. Jamie Overton replaces Sam Curran.

SIX! 50 UP FOR THE WINDIES! Will Jacks gives this one some more flight, full but down the leg side. Shimron Hetmyer sits down on one knee, picks it up and smacks it over the deep backward square leg fence for half a dozen more. 19 runs off Jacks' first over.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.6: Will Jacks to Shimron Hetmyer, Six!

Commentary.Commentary: Goes a bit short and around middle, Roston Chase nudges it through mid-wicket for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.5: Will Jacks to Roston Chase, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Make that three in a row! Will Jacks sees the batter back away, bowls this quicker but this is a full toss, on middle. Roston Chase swings through the line and gets enough power to clear Harry Brook at mid off for four more runs.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.4: Will Jacks to Roston Chase, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! TWO IN TWO! Flatter, full and on middle. Roston Chase goes down across on his knee and sweeps it all along the ground to the deep square leg fence for another boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.3: Will Jacks to Roston Chase, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Takes the aerial route, does Roston Chase! Floated, full and around off. Chase makes room by moving to the leg side. He extends his arms to get under it and lofts it over mid off for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.2: Will Jacks to Roston Chase, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Tossed up, full and on middle, Roston Chase knocks it towards the bowler.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.1: Will Jacks to Roston Chase, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Just the over West Indies needed to get a move on. The pitch has runs written all over it and Hetmyer looks in a fine touch. And here's spin. Brook tosses the ball to Will Jacks, who replaces Jofra Archer from this end.
Bangs in a bouncer, on middle and leg, Roston Chase rolls his wrists and pulls it through square leg for one. 14 runs off the over!
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.6: Sam Curran to Roston Chase, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Hard length and on middle, nips back in a bit. Shimron Hetmyer looks to punch it away but gets an inside edge just past the stumps and towards short fine. They cross.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.5: Sam Curran to Shimron Hetmyer, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Easy pickings! Sam Curran errs in line and serves this full but down the leg side. Shimron Hetmyer just has to get some bat on it and he tickles it away to the fine leg fence for an easy boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.4: Sam Curran to Shimron Hetmyer, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: SIX! BANG! He connects well this time. This is another slower delivery, full and on off. Shimron Hetmyer picks it up early, gets low on his knee and nails the slog sweep over the deep mid-wicket fence for a biggie.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.3: Sam Curran to Shimron Hetmyer, Six!

Commentary.Commentary: In the air...SAFE! Sam Curran dishes out a clever slower one, but it is not the moon ball. Full and around off. Shimron Hetmyer crouches low for the slog across the line, but has to wait an eternity. He does not get it from the middle and the ball goes in the air, but lands well wide of the deep square leg fielder. Phil Salt scoots across and gathers it in the outfield. Two taken.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.2: Sam Curran to Shimron Hetmyer, 2 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: Lands this on a good length and on middle, Shimron Hetmyer stays inside his crease and keeps it out onto the pitch.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.1: Sam Curran to Shimron Hetmyer, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Bowls this into the surface, on off, gets some extra bounce. Roston Chase hops up to get on top of it and pats it towards point again.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.6: Jofra Archer to Roston Chase, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Hits the length hard, on off, Roston Chase stays back and dabs it down to point.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.5: Jofra Archer to Roston Chase, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Shot of the match so far! Jofra Archer goes a bit too full this time, around off. Roston Chase bends his back knee, leans onto his drive and creams it through extra cover for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.4: Jofra Archer to Roston Chase, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Nails the wide yorker, outside off, Roston Chase is very late to get his bat down in time and fails to dig it out.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.3: Jofra Archer to Roston Chase, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Back of a length and on middle, angling into the body of the batter. Shimron Hetmyer looks to pull but gets cramped up for room and misses. It goes off his upper body towards square leg. A leg bye taken.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.2: Jofra Archer to Shimron Hetmyer, Leg bye.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Up and over! Short of a length and outside off. Shimron Hetmyer uses the width on offer, frees his arms and crunches it over point for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.1: Jofra Archer to Shimron Hetmyer, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: A bit fuller and on middle, Roston Chase knocks it back to the bowler. Just 2 runs and a wicket from Curran's first over!
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.6: Sam Curran to Roston Chase, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Good-length delivery, on middle, Roston Chase stays back and blocks it out.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.5: Sam Curran to Roston Chase, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Sam Curran changes his angle and comes over the wicket, lands this full, on middle and leg. Roston Chase looks to flick it away but misses and gets hit on the pads. There is a shout for LBW, but turned down. Harry Brook has a chat with his bowler and keeper, but does not take the review. It looked to be going down the leg side and also pitching outside leg as well.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.4: Sam Curran to Roston Chase, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Back of a length and outside off, Roston Chase slashes his bat at but gets an underedge. It goes on two bounces to the keeper.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.3: Sam Curran to Roston Chase, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Fuller delivery, on off, shaping in, Roston Chase looks to push it away but gets an inside edge through mid-wicket for a couple of runs.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.2: Sam Curran to Roston Chase, 2 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: Both the West Indian openers are back in the hut inside two overs. In walks Roston Chase at number 4.

OUT! TAKEN IN THE DEEP! Sam Curran just cannot do anything wrong with the ball in this World Cup. He begins with a fuller delivery, outside off, again not a wicket-taking delivery. Brandon King sees this as a scoring opportunity and goes after it, but there is a fielder set at deep point for this shot. King cannot control his shot and slices it aerially towards that fielder, where Phil Salt runs forward and dives to take a fantastic catch, scooping the ball cleanly before the ground. England right on top early doors.
Commentary.Howout: c Phil Salt b Sam Curran
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.1: Sam Curran to Brandon King, OUT! c Phil Salt b Sam Curran.

Commentary.Commentary: A very profitable start for England. 8 runs and the fall of Hope from it. Sam Curran to operate from the opposite end.
BEAUTY! Jofra Archer lands this back of a length and in that channel outside off, holds its line. Shimron Hetmyer has a poke at it from the crease but gets beaten on the outside edge.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.6: Jofra Archer to Shimron Hetmyer, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Archer was 'Hope'ful to make amends this time around, and he does in the very first over. Shimron Hetmyer marks his guard as he is in at number 3. A slip in place.

OUT! STRAIGHT TO THE FIELDER! Jofra Archer draws first blood. Not his best delivery, but he won't mind getting a wicket on it. This is short and wide outside off, there to be put away. Shai Hope reaches out and cuts it hard but fails to keep it down and also does not get enough elevation. The ball actually moves away slightly and kicks up a bit. It flies off the splice, straight to cover, where Tom Banton takes a good catch near his midriff. A three-baller for the Windies skipper, and they are rocked early.
Commentary.Howout: c Tom Banton b Jofra Archer
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.5: Jofra Archer to Shai Hope, OUT! c Tom Banton b Jofra Archer.

Commentary.Commentary: Hard length and on middle, nips back in, Shai Hope pushes it out towards cover.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.4: Jofra Archer to Shai Hope, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: WIDE! Tries the bouncer now, but this is a bit too high, on middle. Shai Hope ducks under it. Another wide called.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.4: Jofra Archer to Shai Hope, Wide!

Commentary.Commentary: FIVE WIDES! That beats everyone! Jofra Archer bangs this into the pitch, but way outside off, it keeps on rising and shapes away too. Shai Hope leaves it alone. Jos Buttler, the keeper, moves to his right but has no chance of stopping that. Jamie Overton at first slip, gets fingertips on it above his head but the ball still goes through to the fence behind for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.4: Jofra Archer to Shai Hope, 5 Wides!

Commentary.Commentary: Goes a bit fuller and on off, angling in, Shai Hope stays back and stabs it to the left of the bowler.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.3: Jofra Archer to Shai Hope, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: First runs off the bat! Short of a length and well outside off, Brandon King throws his bat at it. Gets it from the toe-end as the ball rolls towards deep third for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.2: Jofra Archer to Brandon King, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Much better! This is on a good length and on middle and off, Brandon King gets behind the line of it and blocks it out.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.1: Jofra Archer to Brandon King, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: WIDE! Jofra Archer will have to reload it. He steams in from over the wicket, starts with a good-length delivery, but just angling down the leg side. Brandon King fails to tuck it away. Called a wide.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.1: Jofra Archer to Brandon King, Wide!

Commentary.Commentary: Always a matter of pride to sing/chant the national anthem on such occasions, in front of thousands of spectators. The two umpires make their way out to the middle. The Wankhede, as usual, is buzzing with a packed house. They just love the cricket here, be it any team playing. The English players spread out to take their respective spots. Brandon King ​​​and Shai Hope are the two West Indian openers, making their way to the crease. Jofra Archer has the new ball in hand. Had a pretty rough stint against Nepal in the first game. King to take the strike. The slips are empty. Here we go!

Right. We are just a few minutes away from the first ball. But before that, Carlos Brathwaite is given the honor of carrying the glittering trophy out to the middle. He places it carefully on the pedestal. Now, the giant flags of both countries are unfurled in the center as both teams walk out for their national anthems. Rally 'Round the West Indies will play first, followed by the English national anthem.

The skipper of West Indies - Shai Hope says that they would have bowled first as well but now have to set the tone with the bat. Adds that they play against England a lot and they both know what the other is capable of, but this is an important match and they need to bring their A-game. Mentions that they have made one tactical change, bringing in Roston Chase for Matthew Forde. Ends by saying Chase's off-break can come in handy against the left-handers of the English team.

The captain of England - Harry Brook says that the stats favors the teams batting second here and cites that is the very reason to bowl first. On the learnings from the Nepal game, he says it is all about staying cool and sticking to the same game plan and processes. Informs that there is one change in their XI as Jamie Overton replaces Luke Wood as they opt to lengthen their batting a bit.

West Indies (Playing XI) - Shai Hope (C/WK), Brandon King, Shimron Hetmyer, Rovman Powell, Sherfane Rutherford, Roston Chase (In place of Matthew Forde), Jason Holder, Romario Shepherd, Akeal Hosein, Gudakesh Motie, Shamar Joseph.
England (Playing XI) - Phil Salt, Jos Buttler (WK), Jacob Bethell, Tom Banton, Harry Brook (C), Sam Curran, Will Jacks, Liam Dawson, Jamie Overton (In place of Luke Wood), Jofra Archer, Adil Rashid.

TOSS - It is time for the coin-flip here in Mumbai. Both the captains, Harry Brook and Shai Hope are out there in the middle with Ian Bishop presenting the toss. Brook gives it a flip, and Hope calls 'Heads' but it comes down as 'Tails'. England elect to BOWL first.

PITCH REPORT - Samuel Badree says it is a bit warm out there but the conditions are pleasant with the temperature being 30 degrees and the humidity around 40 percent. Also adds that there is a very gentle breeze blowing across the stadium, which might provide some respite for the players. About the dimensions, he points out that it is 64 and 65 meters on the square boundaries, and the straight hit is 75 meters. Nasser Hussain joins and gives his impressions on the surface and informs that it is a fresh strip. Also highlights that the first two games were played on pitch number 8, where the ball gripped a bit for the seamers in the first game, pointing out Shadley van Schalkwyk's variations, and the spinners got a good purchase in the Nepal game. About the current surface, Nasser mentions that it is a fresh one with a good covering of grass. Also observes a few bare patches but reckons it is still a better surface and will stay true. Expects the ball to come nicely onto the bat. Points that England might be playing Overton because they want somebody to come in and hit the pitch really hard, which he does effectively. Then goes on to mention that both sides have a good quality of spin and big hitters, expecting this to be a cracker of a game.

Game over - That match in Colombo is now done and dusted, with Australia bowling Ireland out for 115 to seal a commanding 67-run victory. It leaves Ireland staring at two defeats from two, and their path to the knockout stages now looks incredibly slim. To compound their troubles, their captain, Paul Stirling picked up an injury in the very first over of the chase and was unable to come out and bat, and if he is ruled out for the rest of the tournament, their task only gets tougher from here.

What's happening elsewhere? While we wait for the toss here, over in Colombo Australia are closing in on a winning start to their World Cup campaign against Ireland. Choosing to bat, they piled up 182 thanks to fluent contributions from Inglis and Stoinis, and in reply Ireland have slipped to 112 for 8 in 16 overs, with Dockrell the lone resistor as Adam Zampa's spin has ripped through the middle order with a four-wicket haul. You can just switch tabs to enjoy our coverage of that game as well.

Blast from the past - The last time England and West Indies crossed paths in a T20 World Cup at the Wankhede Stadium, in 2016, Chris Gayle set the stage ablaze with a brutal unbeaten hundred off just 48 balls, and with explosive hitters stacked on both sides this time as well, the chances of another run-fest feel very real. Whether it is a moment of individual brilliance or a full-blown batting onslaught, all signs point towards a night of high drama. Stay tuned for the toss and other updates to what promises to be a blockbuster contest.

West Indies blend form with fearless history - West Indies have started this tournament with the kind of energy that reflects their T20 identity, built around big-hitting from Hetmyer, Powell and Rutherford and wicket-taking threats like Shepherd, whose hat-trick in the opener was a sharp reminder of how quickly they can turn a game. That firepower is matched by a strong record against England in T20 World Cups, where they have won five of seven encounters, giving them both confidence and pedigree heading into another high-profile clash.

England tested, but still in control - A narrow victory in their first match showed both England's depth and their resilience, with Brook and Bethell doing the hard work before Curran delivered at the death. They also arrive with recent success against West Indies, having beaten them in their last two encounters in T20 World Cups, which gives them an edge in confidence. But the memory of Carlos Brathwaite's famous night in 2016 remains part of this rivalry, a reminder that no lead is ever truly safe against the Caribbean side.

Battle of Heavyweights - Welcome to what promises to be one of the marquee clashes of the group stage as England versus West Indies brings together two former champions in a game that could go a long way in shaping the qualification places. Both sides are coming in with momentum, and with the chance to grab top spot, this clash carries far more than just bragging rights, as one win here could push them nearer to the Super Six stage, while defeat will only make things harder.
... MATCH DAY ...

Past Glory, Present Fight - 'Carlos Brathwaite, Carlos Brathwaite, remember the name' - those immortal words from Ian Bishop still ring in the ears of every cricket fan, probably except the English, and especially Ben Stokes, who was on the receiving end of four straight sixes that sealed West Indies' second T20 World Cup at the iconic Eden Gardens back in 2016, and now, almost a decade later, the same two sides meet again in another legendary Indian venue, the Wankhede Stadium in Mumbai, as England and West Indies lock horns in a blockbuster Group C clash of the ICC T20 World Cup 2026. When two teams who between them own four of the last eight T20 World Cup trophies face off, history does not whisper, it roars, and that is exactly the feeling around this match, with the Windies at the top and England third, Scotland in between them and only net run-rate separating the trio, making every run count even more with the winner set to go top and take control of the group. England's balancing act - England arrive with both confidence and a warning label after scraping past Nepal in a thriller that almost slipped away, rescued only by Sam Curran's ice-cold final over and Will Jacks' outstanding all-round display, while Harry Brook, now leading the side in his first ICC tournament since taking over from Jos Buttler, stamped his authority with a gritty half-century, and Jacob Bethell looked born for the big stage at number three with a fluent fifty of his own. Yet, for all that promise, England know their true firepower lies at the top, where Buttler and Phil Salt, the two highest run-scorers for England in T20Is in 2025, have yet to explode, and with Tom Banton also searching for rhythm, this batting unit still feels like a storm waiting to break. The bowling has similar duality, with Adil Rashid eager to bounce back from an off day, Liam Dawson proving his value with a match-shaping spell against Nepal, and the much-vaunted pace duo of Jofra Archer and Luke Wood needing to deliver the kind of new-ball and death-over authority that has defined England's best white-ball teams. Muscle and menace - West Indies, meanwhile, showcased both their muscle and their menace in a convincing win over Scotland, where Shimron Hetmyer's blazing 64 off 36 and the late hitting of Sherfane Rutherford and Rovman Powell dragged them to a daunting total. However, Shai Hope and Brandon King will want to be more proactive in the Powerplay to truly strangle opponents early and they could also look to bring in Johnson Charles to help with that. Their bowling, though, already looks tournament-ready, led by the unforgettable Romario Shepherd, who produced the first hat-trick of this World Cup and a five-wicket haul that included four wickets in a single over, while Akeal Hosein and Gudakesh Motie offer a smart spin combination. Jason Holder brings both experience and history after becoming the first Windies player to reach 100 T20I wickets, and Shamar Joseph's raw pace adds a layer of fear. Team Form (Last 5 T20Is, latest result first) - England - WWWWW | West Indies - WWLLW. Pitch and Conditions - Conditions could add another aspect to this contest, with dew expected in this night game but the new ball still likely to ask plenty of questions, as seen in the India vs USA match where timing was hard to find early and several stroke-makers struggled to get going. While Wankhede is traditionally a high-scoring venue, batters may have to take a few overs to settle before teeing off, especially with the first two games here also showing there is some assistance for seamers and spinners alike, making smart bowling and shot selection just as important as raw power. What to expect? With West Indies' depth, balance and momentum up against England's pedigree and explosiveness, this clash carries layers of history, with the two sides having already met seven times in T20 World Cups, the Windies winning the first five, including the iconic 2016 final and a group game here in Mumbai lit up by Chris Gayle's unforgettable unbeaten 48-ball hundred. England have wrestled back control by winning the last two meetings, one of them a brutal drubbing where Adil Rashid spun a web to bowl the Windies out for just 55, setting the stage for another swing in this long-running rivalry as it is a collision between two past champions determined to prove that the future of T20 cricket still runs through them.
